# zone_ssh_public_key (Resource)

An SSH public key authorised to log in to a webhosting service.

~> **This resource cannot be changed in place.** Its endpoint offers no update operation, so every argument below forces Terraform to destroy and recreate it. That is cheap here — the object carries no data — but it does mean a brief window with the entry absent.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The API cannot modify an authorised key, so changing either argument here
# destroys and recreates it.
resource "zone_ssh_public_key" "deploy" {
  service_name = "virt1.example.com"
  public_key   = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")
  comment      = "Deploy key"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `public_key` (String) The key itself, in OpenSSH format — the one line from a `.pub` file, for example `file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")`.
- `service_name` (String) The webhosting service this belongs to. This is a virtual server name, which often looks like a domain but is a different namespace from a DNS zone — use the `zone_vservers` data source to list the valid values. Changing it moves the resource to another service, which means replacing it.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) A note on the key, shown in the ZoneID panel.

### Read-Only

- `created` (String) When the key was authorised.
- `fingerprint` (String) The key's fingerprint, as zone.eu computed it. Also accepted as an import ID.
- `id` (Number) Numeric identifier assigned by zone.eu.
- `last_used` (String) When the key was last used to log in, or null if it never has been.
- `resource_url` (String) API URL of this key.
- `size` (Number) Key size in bits, where that is meaningful. Null for key types with a fixed size, such as Ed25519.
- `type` (String) Key algorithm, derived from the key itself, for example `ed25519` or `rsa`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Either the numeric id or the fingerprint works, and the fingerprint is the
# one you actually have -- from ssh-keygen -lf ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub.
terraform import zone_ssh_public_key.deploy "virt1.example.com/SHA256:abc123..."
terraform import zone_ssh_public_key.deploy "virt1.example.com/59386"
```
